INC-AIT-V0031.action: Review gateway and integration logs for rate-limit responses, retry exhaustion, or quota-based rejection events.
INC-AIT-V0031.expected: No rate-limit response prevents the integration job from completing.

INC-AIT-V0032.expected: Token validation succeeds and the API accepts authenticated calls.
INC-AIT-V0032.observed: The downstream API token for service account svc-custsync was still valid (expiry 2026-08-01) and authenticated requests from the Integration Gateway were accepted when sent outside the heavy batch burst. Manual test calls from host WORKSTATION-PNAIR-L1 (IP 10.42.17.88) also returned 200 OK.

INC-AIT-V0032.action: Compare integration job timing with API gateway latency and downstream service health.
INC-AIT-V0032.expected: API response latency is within the integration timeout window.
INC-AIT-V0032.observed: Average API latency was generally within the configured 30-second timeout window (p50: 1.2s, p99: 8.4s), but many requests in the batch period were delayed by repeated retries after throttling responses (HTTP 429) rather than by sustained service slowness. Monitoring System dashboards for the us-east-1 region confirmed no infrastructure-level latency spikes.

INC-AIT-V0032.action: Check API gateway logs for rate-limit or retry exhaustion events.
INC-AIT-V0032.expected: No rate-limit response prevents the integration job from completing.
INC-AIT-V0032.observed: Gateway logs showed repeated HTTP 429 and quota-exceeded responses from the downstream API beginning at 2026-05-14T01:22:00Z, followed by retry exhaustion that surfaced to the job runner as timeout failures. Over 3,400 requests were throttled within a 45-minute window.

INC-AIT-V0033.action: Confirm the integration token or secret remained valid for the affected overnight synchronization window.
INC-AIT-V0033.expected: Token validation succeeds and the API accepts authenticated calls.
INC-AIT-V0033.observed: The active downstream API token for service account integration-svc-custsync appeared valid in configuration review (vault path: secret/igw/custsync/api-token, last rotated 2026-04-28). However, only limited authenticated test calls were completed by Priya Nair after the incident window (~05:45 UTC), so full token behavior during the 02:00–03:30 failure period could not be conclusively reproduced. No HTTP 401 or 403 responses were logged.

INC-AIT-V0033.action: Compare failed integration job timing with Integration Gateway latency metrics and downstream service responsiveness.
INC-AIT-V0033.expected: API response latency is within the integration timeout window.
INC-AIT-V0033.observed: Some gateway metrics from igw-gw-east-01.corplabs.internal showed elevated response times near the batch peak (p50 rose from 220ms to 1,400ms; p99 spiked to ~6,200ms against a configured 30s timeout), but trace coverage for the exact failed requests was incomplete (10% sampling rate yielded only 47 captured traces out of ~1,200 requests) and did not establish whether latency alone exceeded the timeout window for all 38 impacted jobs.

INC-AIT-V0033.action: Review API gateway logs for rate-limit responses, retry exhaustion, or throttling indicators during the failure period.
INC-AIT-V0033.expected: No rate-limit response prevents the integration job from completing.
INC-AIT-V0033.observed: Log review on igw-gw-east-01.corplabs.internal found a small number of throttling-related entries (3 HTTP 429 responses with Retry-After headers) mixed with 38 generic timeout errors (504/ETIMEDOUT), but not enough consistent evidence to confirm rate limiting as the primary driver of the incident. The 429 responses occurred at 02:22, 02:47, and 03:08 UTC.

INC-DCP-V0034.action: Compared the assigned compliance policy with the device's intended scope and assignment to rule out stale or incorrect targeting.
INC-DCP-V0034.expected: Device is in the intended policy scope with no stale assignment.
INC-DCP-V0034.observed: The device WORKSTATION-DELL-RN was still assigned to the intended compliance policy (US-Marketing-Compliance-v3) scoped to the Marketing user group, and there was no stale or incorrect policy targeting.

INC-DCP-V0035.action: Confirm the device has recently checked in to endpoint management and whether compliance evaluation has refreshed.
INC-DCP-V0035.expected: Device check-in timestamp is current and compliance evaluation has run.

This caused Intune to continue evaluating devices against stale targeting that required a different encryption reporting format, leaving them incorrectly noncompliant.

INC-DCP-V0036.action: Confirmed recent Intune check-in status and whether a new compliance evaluation had executed on impacted devices.
INC-DCP-V0036.expected: Device check-in timestamp is current and compliance evaluation has run.
INC-DCP-V0036.observed: The device record for WORKSTATION-GALAXY-MD (user: mdelgado) showed a recent check-in at 2026-05-14T22:47:00Z, but the compliance evaluation timestamp (2026-05-14T18:12:00Z) did not clearly indicate whether a full re-evaluation had completed after the latest Conditional Access block at 22:55Z. Rachel Okonkwo's device showed a similar gap between check-in and evaluation timestamps.

INC-DCP-V0036.action: Reviewed the failing compliance signal to determine why devices were being marked noncompliant.
INC-DCP-V0036.expected: Required compliance signals report healthy values.
